items.title: Democratic wave sweeps suburban Illinois, toppling longtime Republican officeholders
items.summary: Tuesday’s elections saw a broad defeat of Illinois Republicans in traditionally GOP suburbs, including state Sens. Seth Lewis of Bartlett, Craig Lewis of McHenry, and Darby Hills of Barrington Hills. The district of outgoing Sen. Don DeWitte of St. Charles also flipped to Democrats, and in the House Republicans Martin McLaughlin, Jennifer Sanalitro and Dan Ugaste lost their seats. The results suggest national political dynamics impacted even moderate suburban districts.

items.title: Illinois House Speaker Chris Welch announces he will not seek another term
items.summary: Speaker Emanuel “Chris” Welch said Thursday he will step down after 26 House Democrats called for new leadership, ending his tenure as leader of the Democratic supermajority. He will help select his successor as the chamber enters a new session in January with a record‑setting 85‑member Democratic majority. Welch’s decision follows criticism over his handling of sexual‑harassment allegations involving former Rep. Harry Benton.

items.title: Democratic wave sweeps Illinois suburban Republicans in November elections
items.summary: Tuesday’s election results showed a sizable roster of Illinois Republicans losing seats in traditionally GOP suburbs, including state Sens. Seth Lewis of Bartlett, Craig Lewis of McHenry, and Darby Hills of Barrington Hills. The district of outgoing Sen. Don DeWitte of St. Charles flipped to Democrats, and in the House Democrat Erica Bray‑Parker captured the 47th District vacated by Rep. Amy Grant. The losses suggest national political fallout reached moderate suburban voters.

items.title: Jessica Biggs wins Chicago school board presidency as Rahm Emanuel declares victory

items.title: Cindy Bailey confronts Gov. JB Pritzker over campaign attacks ahead of Illinois governor race

JB Pritzker’s ads that she says mischaracterize her husband’s views on women. She highlighted her 40‑year marriage, family farm, and her own floral shop as evidence of her husband’s respect for women, and warned that the attacks also disparage stay‑at‑home mothers. items.title: State legislators introduce EDGE Essentials bill to expand tax credits for independent pharmacies and grocery stores

Doris Turner announced legislation called EDGE Essentials that would broaden the existing EDGE tax credit program to attract and grow independent pharmacies and grocery stores across Illinois. items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson turned in roughly 33,000 signatures to the Chicago Board of Elections on Friday, meeting the 12,500‑signature requirement to appear on the ballot. items.title: Gov. JB Pritzker receives United Auto Workers endorsement at South Side rally
items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker shook hands with United Auto Workers members after the union endorsed him on Oct. 25, 2026, during a rally on Chicago’s South Side. Pritzker highlighted the Big Three strike that began in 2023 and framed his campaign as a fight for better wages and benefits for workers. The endorsement comes as the governor and Republican challenger Darren Bailey intensify their outreach ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

items.title: What's up with Bally's graffiti?
items.summary: Graffiti on the exterior of Bally's Chicago hotel tower has sat untouched for at least two months, becoming emblematic of the casino project's construction delays. Bally's has faced a series of setbacks in its River West casino, hotel and entertainment project. Its August announcement that it was pausing work added another wrinkle in the long-awaited project that promises to pour about $200 million into city.

items.title: CTA Pink and Green Line service interruptions continue through Oct 28 due to Lake Street Bridge work
items.summary: The CTA announced that because of additional work on the new leaf of the Lake Street Bridge, Pink and Green Line service between the Clinton and Clark/Lake stations will be suspended until 4 a.m. on October 28. Free bus substitutions will run between those stations, and Green Line trains will operate in two sections with all‑stop service on each side of the disruption. items.title: 1133 W. Kinzie development moves forward with new Pizzeria Gabbo
items.summary: The West Loop development at 1133 W. Kinzie is progressing, adding a new pizza, pasta and gelato venue called Pizzeria Gabbo in Fulton Market. The project expands dining options in the neighborhood and reflects ongoing commercial growth in the area.

items.summary: Oct. 26 is the final day for Chicago mayoral candidates to file nominating petitions with the Chicago Board of Elections. Candidates need 12,500 valid signatures, and the deadline to file objections to other candidates' petitions is Nov. 2. Mayor Brandon Johnson filed roughly 33,000 signatures on Friday, and Alexi Giannoulias, Mike Quigley, Willie Wilson, John Kelly and Matt Brewer are already in the race, with Comptroller Susana Mendoza expected to file today.

items.title: Kennedy Expressway commutes remain slow three years after the rehab began
items.summary: A WBEZ analysis found most of the longest Kennedy Expressway commutes on record happened during the three-year rehab project, as the state spent more than $170 million on the 7.5-mile stretch between Downtown and the Edens junction. items.title: Midterm campaign enters its final week as Republicans brace for House losses

President Trump holds a rally in Mississippi on Monday, a state where Democrats see a rare Senate opening.

items.title: Graffiti on Bally's River West tower highlights casino construction delays
items.summary: Graffiti on the exterior of the Bally's Chicago hotel tower near Grand Avenue has gone untouched for at least two months. Bally's paused work on nongaming amenities in August amid a dispute with the city over the 2026 budget's legalization of video gambling terminals, and says crews are now focused on the casino floor. The project is expected to send about $200 million a year to city pension funds.

items.title: Judges fill most of the Chicago midterm ballot: how retention votes work
items.summary: Most questions on Chicago's Nov. 3 ballot involve judges, with more than 60 Cook County judges up for retention. Retained judges need 60% approval, and only three have failed to win retention in the last six years. Voter guides with recommendations are available from the Chicago Bar Association and the Illinois Alliance of Bar Associations.

items.title: Free WCA member workshop Oct. 27: build a 90-day plan for your business
items.summary: The West Central Association is hosting a free, hands-on working session for member business owners on Tuesday, Oct. 27, led by Dan Brown, The Growth Coach of West Loop/Chicagoland. Participants will look at revenue per hour, where revenue comes from and how their time is spent, then leave with a written 90-day plan. Seating is limited and RSVP is required.

items.title: Homerathon brings a full read-aloud of The Odyssey to Greektown Oct. 29-30
items.summary: The National Hellenic Museum in Greektown and UIC's Department of Classics and Mediterranean Studies are reading Homer's Odyssey aloud from beginning to end on Thursday, Oct. 29 (12:30-8 p.m.) and Friday, Oct. 30 (10 a.m.-4 p.m.). A Thursday happy hour from 6-8 p.m. invites visitors to grab a drink and read a passage. The museum's exhibit The Odyssey Reimagined is also on view Thursdays through Sundays.

items.title: Pink and Green Line closure at Lake Street Bridge extended to Oct. 28

Free shuttle buses continue between Clinton and Clark/Lake, and Green Line trains run in two sections. Pink Line riders should transfer to the Blue Line at Racine, or take the 9/X9 Ashland bus to reach Ashland, Morgan, Clinton and the West Loop.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson pushes citywide head tax despite business opposition
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson began a citywide tour Thursday to promote his budget proposal, emphasizing a head tax that the business community has opposed. Critics warn the tax could drive businesses out of Chicago, while Johnson argued no corporation is leaving and that people are being forced out because schools have closed or safety concerns. His rival Alexi Giannoulias offered an alternative plan to cut $4.5 billion in contract spending and collect more of the $8 billion owed in fines and fees.

items.title: Governor Pritzker’s BUILD Act aims to loosen zoning for more housing
items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker highlighted the BUILD Act during a briefing on the upcoming veto session, saying it would make it easier to build more housing by loosening local zoning rules, allowing more multifamily homes and backyard apartments, and streamlining the development process. The proposal has raised questions about how much authority the state would take from local governments. The act is expected to be considered in the short six‑day veto session starting Nov. 17.

items.title: Sepia x Zaragoza Eight‑Course Collaborative Tasting Menu

Milwaukee Street is closed from Canal to Fulton until October 30.

items.title: O'Hare Flyer Transportation Project to Connect Chicago and O’Hare International Airport
items.summary: The WCA Speaker Series will discuss the proposed O'Hare Flyer transportation project on November 17 at The Green at 320, offering a Q&A about the plan to link downtown Chicago with O’Hare International Airport. The event will bring together community members and experts to explore the project's impact on transit and local development.

items.title: Federal Reserve Launches 2026 Small Business Credit Survey for Chicago Businesses
items.summary: The WCA partners with the Federal Reserve to conduct a 12‑minute confidential survey open through November 13, gathering data on financing, debt, and business conditions from owners and key financial decision makers of for‑profit businesses in Chicago. The survey's findings will inform policymakers, service providers, and government agencies about the needs of small businesses.

items.title: Another suspicious letter delivered to government building downtown Chicago, officials say
items.summary: Chicago firefighters responded yet again after a suspicious letter was sent to a federal building in the city.

items.title: Oh, Mary!' Chicago Tickets On Sale Now
items.summary: The Tony Award-winning Broadway hit is coming to CIBC Theatre in January, but J. Harrison Ghee won't be performing as Mary Todd Lincoln. A replacement has yet to be announced.

items.title: Gov. Pritzker focuses on Bears stadium deal and ethics reform ahead of short veto session
items.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker told reporters the priority for the upcoming six‑day veto session starting Nov. 17 is a deal to keep the Chicago Bears in Illinois, with the team weighing options for a new stadium. He also signaled low expectations for sweeping legislation, noting ethics reform may have to wait until January. Proposals under discussion include the POWER Act for data‑center energy costs and the BUILD Act to loosen zoning for multifamily housing.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson defends head tax amid business opposition during citywide budget tour
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson launched a citywide tour on Thursday, doubling down on a proposed head tax that business groups say could drive firms out of Chicago. Johnson argued no corporation is leaving, but warned that school closures and safety concerns are forcing residents out. His rival Alexi Giannoulias offered an alternative plan to cut $4.5 billion in contracts and collect more fines and fees.

items.title: CTA Loop Elevated track repairs shut down Loop stations Oct. 24‑26
items.summary: The Chicago Transit Authority will close Loop Elevated stations from Saturday, Oct. 24 at 4 a.m. until Monday, Oct. 26 at 2 a.m. to perform track repairs. Shuttle buses will serve the Green, Orange and Brown lines, and the Green, Pink, Orange and Brown lines will run on shortened routes with free bus substitutions. The service changes affect commuters in the Loop, West Loop and surrounding neighborhoods.

items.title: West Loop Green City Market continues Saturdays but office will not table for rest of season
items.summary: The West Loop Green City Market operates Saturdays from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at 900 W. Monroe, bringing dozens of local farmers and food producers to the neighborhood. Market staff announced they will not be tabling at the market for the remainder of the season due to upcoming fall events.

items.title: Arts in the Dark Parade scheduled for Oct. 24 in the Loop
items.summary: The Arts in the Dark Parade will begin at 6 p.m. on Saturday, Oct. 24, marching from Columbus and Balbo north to Monroe. The event showcases the State Street arts and culture community ahead of Halloween and includes street closures and parking restrictions along the route.

items.title: Pizzeria Gabbo Opens at 1133 W. Kinzie in Fulton Market
items.summary: Pizzeria Gabbo, a new pizza, pasta, and gelato spot, has opened at 1133 W. Kinzie in Fulton Market. The restaurant is part of the West Central Association’s list of Chicago’s best Italian restaurants. It offers a menu featuring pizza, pasta, and gelato.

items.title: Sepia x Zaragoza Eight-Course Tasting Menu
items.summary: Chef Jonathan Zaragoza will join Chef Kyle Cottle for an eight-course menu at Sepia on November 4. The dinner will be held at 123 North Jefferson St, Chicago, IL 60661, and tickets cost $195 per person. The menu blends Zaragoza’s Mexican culinary heritage with Cottle’s contemporary, ingredient-driven approach.

items.title: Suspicious letter draws hazmat response at Kluczynski Federal Building in downtown Chicago Friday morning
items.summary: The Chicago Fire Department's hazmat team responded to the Kluczynski Federal Building for a suspicious letter Friday morning.

items.title: Fitness Friday: Bar Method in South Loop
items.summary: Bar Method in the South Loop offers classes to build muscle, strengthen your core and improve flexibility and balance with a combination of movement inspired by pilates and yoga with ballet barre training.

items.title: Gino's East celebrates 60 years of Chicago deep dish pizza
items.summary: Gino's East in downtown Chicago is celebrating 60 years of family owned and operated deep dish pizza joy.

items.title: Chicago's 13 Most Haunted Places Share A Spooky History
items.summary: A devil baby, unexplained voices and shadowy figures have all been reported at some of Chicago's most historic institutions.

items.title: Manhattan Vintage show comes to Morgan Manufacturing in Fulton Market this weekend
items.summary: Manhattan Vintage, a New York vintage clothing show running since 1992, holds its Chicago edition Saturday, Oct. 24 and Sunday, Oct. 25 at Morgan Manufacturing in Fulton Market. Hours are 1:30 to 6 p.m. Saturday and 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Sunday, and tickets start at $25. Co-owner Amy Abrams grew up in Highland Park, making the show a homecoming.

items.title: Brazil heads to a presidential runoff Sunday with Flavio Bolsonaro favored
items.summary: Brazil holds its presidential runoff on Sunday, Oct. 25, with polls suggesting Flavio Bolsonaro is on course to defeat President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva after taking a narrow first-round lead. POLITICO Forecast notes no Brazilian candidate has ever come back from a first-round defeat, though polls have narrowed. Serbia also holds snap parliamentary elections the same day.

items.title: Gov. Pritzker eyes legislation to keep Chicago Bears in Illinois, potential stadium deal
items.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker said he is encouraging lawmakers to pass legislation that would clear a path for the Bears to build a new stadium in Illinois. The Bears are weighing options as they search for a new home, and the governor hopes a deal will emerge during the short veto session that begins on Nov. 17. Pritzker kept expectations low, noting only a few specific items are likely to be addressed.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson defends controversial head tax amid business opposition
items.summary: Mayor Brandon Johnson launched a citywide tour to sell his budget proposal and doubled down on a head tax that business leaders oppose. Critics warn the tax could drive businesses out of Chicago, while Johnson said no corporation is leaving but people are being forced out by school closures and safety concerns. His rival Alexi Giannoulias offered an alternative plan to cut $4.5 billion in contract spending and collect more fines and fees.

items.title: Data centers projected to cost ComEd $3 billion, raising consumer concerns
items.summary: Expert testimony to the Illinois Commerce Commission indicated that data centers will cost ComEd about $3 billion, with the utility having collected roughly $721 million in deposits from developers. Consumer groups warned that Illinois households could be on the hook for the expense. The testimony highlighted the financial impact of large data centers on the state's electricity infrastructure.

items.summary: The Arts in the Dark Parade begins at 6 p.m. on Saturday Oct. 24, marching from Columbus and Balbo north to Monroe. items.title: Pizzeria Gabbo Opens in Fulton Market, Featured Among Chicago’s Best Italian Restaurants
items.summary: Pizzeria Gabbo, a new Italian restaurant in Fulton Market, has been highlighted by the West Central Association as one of Chicago’s best Italian eateries. The restaurant offers pizza, pasta, and gelato and is located on 1133 W. Kinzie. The WCA’s recognition underscores the growing culinary scene in the West Loop.

items.title: Chicago Restaurant Week 2027 Opens Registration for 20th Annual Event
items.summary: The 20th annual Chicago Restaurant Week will run from January 22 to February 7, 2027, offering restaurants a chance to boost visibility and revenue. Partners of Choose Chicago must register by October 28, 2026, to participate. The event is a key seasonal highlight for the city’s dining scene.

items.summary: Film producer Pam Kasper is fundraising for a bronze statue of the film critics, to be made by Illinois sculptor Preston Jackson and placed at Prudential Plaza in 2028.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson unveils 2027 Fair Share Budget with corporate head tax and $664 million in new revenue
items.summary: The mayor announced a budget that would raise $664.2 million from large corporations through a $25‑per‑employee head tax, a 15‑cent tax on single‑use mailers, and a higher cloud tax, while projecting $840 million in savings. Funding would expand Chicago Youth Works to hire 40,000 summer workers, add $40.6 million for violence intervention, $15 million for homelessness services, $13 million for rental assistance, and $2.5 million for a Jackson Park homeowner tax‑relief pilot, all without raising property taxes.

items.title: Mary Bartelme Park hosts family Halloween celebration on Oct. 31
items.summary: The 34th Ward team and the Mary Bartelme Park Advisory Council will hold a Halloween celebration at Mary Bartelme Park on Oct. 31 from 9:30 a.m. to 11:30 a.m. located at 115 S. Sangamon. The event will feature live music, a balloon artist, and other spooky activities for families.

items.title: Randolph Row Holiday Stroll returns Dec. 10 with shop deals in West Loop
items.summary: The annual Randolph Row Holiday Stroll will take place on Dec. 10, inviting shoppers to explore West Loop businesses along Randolph Row. Participating stores will offer special discounts and promotions all day, and businesses can sign up through the provided participation form.

items.summary: Halloween fun, a hops harvest festival and Día de los Muertos celebrations are also on deck.

items.title: Mexican Mr. Beef? Stand That Inspired The Bear' Hosts Pop-Up With Michelin Chef
items.summary: Acclaimed London chef Santiago Lastra is partnering with the River North beef stand, "The Bear" crew and actor Will Poulter for Sunday's event featuring a spin on Italian beef, made with beef tongue.

items.title: After 1,000-plus bird collisions in one weekend, advocates push a bird-friendly building law
items.summary: More than 1,000 migrating birds were killed or injured in building collisions in Chicago last weekend, and Chicago Bird Collision Monitors collected more than 700 dead birds. Advocates are renewing calls for the Bird-Friendly Building Design Ordinance, which would require bird-safe glass or permanent window markers on new buildings and major facade work, but not on single-family homes or two- and three-flats. Until then, residents and businesses in tall buildings can help by putting lights on timers or motion sensors and drawing blinds at night.

items.title: Pizzeria Gabbo opens today in the former Beatrix Market space in Fulton Market
items.summary: Lettuce Entertain You is replacing Beatrix Market, which closed this summer, with Pizzeria Gabbo, serving pizza by the slice and other menu items starting today. Axios also rounded up fall closures elsewhere in the city, including the River North Hooters at 660 N. Wells St. after 35 years, Southport Grocery in Lakeview at year end, and West Town brunch spot Flo in December.

items.title: Business groups and 2027 mayoral candidates line up against proposed head tax and cloud tax hike
items.summary: The Chicagoland Chamber of Commerce says it will join the Civic Committee of the Commercial Club to block the proposed $25-per-employee monthly head tax and an increase in the personal property lease ("cloud") tax from 15% to 20%. Mayoral candidates Alexi Giannoulias, Mike Quigley, Willie Wilson and Susana Mendoza all criticized the budget, with Mendoza objecting to $480 million in proposed borrowing for police settlements. The plan also includes 40,000 summer youth jobs, $40.6 million for violence intervention and 10 new forestry crews.

items.title: How Israel's election could shape the Iran war
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast previews Israel's Tuesday election, where polls show Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc narrowly trailing former army chief Gadi Eisenkot's. Analysts expect little change on Gaza policy under Eisenkot but a tougher line on violent West Bank settlers and a less hawkish stance on Iran. The newsletter also covers Ukraine's request for an extra 70 billion euros in 2027 defense funding from European allies.

items.title: The Oct. 21 Skyline is out
items.summary: The Oct. 21 edition of Skyline is out. In his note to readers, editor Tom O'Gorman says the city is busy with galas and charitable work, which he calls the real Chicago story of hardworking, generous people.

items.title: Mayor Brandon Johnson proposes $664 million corporate head tax in 2027 Fair Share Budget
items.summary: Johnson unveiled a 2027 Fair Share Budget that would raise $664.2 million from large corporations through a $25‑per‑employee head tax and a 15‑cent fee on single‑use mailers, plus higher personal‑property lease taxes on big‑tech firms. The plan promises $840 million in projected savings and earmarks $40.6 million for community violence intervention, $15 million for homelessness services, $13 million for rental assistance, and $2.5 million for a Jackson Park homeowner tax‑relief pilot. It also seeks to fund Chicago Youth Works to hire 40,000 summer workers and double funding for the Streets and Sanitation Quality of Life program, all without raising property taxes.

items.title: Alders pick apart Mayor's budget
items.summary: Moments after leaving Mayor Brandon Johnson's budget address Wednesday, alders offered takes that ranged from robust support to claims that Johnson's budget is "imbalanced. " The yawning divide suggests a long, grueling and ultra-political budget season ahead as Johnson and the council try to close an $882 million gap while running for reelection. What's inside: Mayoral critics say Johnson has proposed.

items.title: Chicago police issue warning about thieves posing as fundraisers for charity groups downtown
items.summary: A warning about thieves posing as fundraisers for charity groups has been issued by Chicago police. They've hit at least eight spots in just the past two weeks, mostly near businesses in the Loop.

items.summary: The incidents occurred at restaurants in the Loop, West Loop and Near South Side during various hours of the day between Oct. 7 and 18.

items.summary: A developer is seeking to build a five-story, 24-unit building on the property where the iconic diner stood for more than 85 years.

items.title: Midwest Performance Cars becomes official Toys for Tots drop‑off site
items.summary: Starting Monday, November 2, Midwest Performance Cars at 2105 W Fulton St will accept donated toys for the Toys for Tots program. The shop invites the West Loop community to drop off items throughout the holiday season.

items.title: Montessori Academy of Chicago hosts open house on Nov. 7
items.summary: The Montessori Academy of Chicago will hold an open house on Saturday, November 7 from 12:00 to 1:30 p.m. Prospective families can tour the school, meet staff, and learn about its programs.

items.title: Chicago's Thriller' Flash Mob Bigger Than Ever After 14 Years
items.summary: The dance group started as a pop-up in 2012 with seven dancers. Now, more than 160 people will be performing the “Thriller” dance at the Haunted Halsted Halloween Parade on Oct. 31.

items.title: What a post-midterm White House could mean for foreign policy
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast looks at how presidents facing a divided Congress often turn their attention abroad, and what that could mean after the Nov. 3 midterms, from Ukraine and Iran to NATO troop levels. The newsletter also reports that Michael Bloomberg is spending at least $80 million to help Democratic candidates in the final stretch. Ukraine's president said U.S. intelligence-sharing has resumed after talks in Oslo.

items.title: Proposed pilot would let low-income residents seek relief on $200 city sticker tickets
items.summary: An ordinance filed Tuesday at City Council would create a pilot program letting low-income Chicagoans apply for a waiver or reduction of the city's $200 city sticker ticket based on financial need. It was filed by City Clerk Anna Valencia with Alds. Matt Martin (47th) and Nicole Lee (11th). The Clerk's office is also working on a three-month amnesty program.

items.title: Senate debate pits Democrat Juliana Stratton against Republican Don Tracy
items.summary: The Illinois U.S. Senate debate on Oct. 20 featured Democratic Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton and Republican Don Tracy discussing Trump’s influence, the war in Iran, energy policy, a $25 federal minimum wage, Medicare for All, and immigration enforcement. Stratton linked rising costs to Trump’s policies and called for a $25 minimum wage and Medicare for All, while Tracy warned that a higher minimum wage would hurt small businesses and advocated for expanded domestic energy production. The debate was moderated by Brandis Friedman and highlighted the candidates’ contrasting foreign‑policy and economic approaches.

items.title: Two SEIU locals endorse Alexi Giannoulias for Chicago mayor
items.summary: SEIU Local 73 and another chapter announced on Tuesday that they are backing Alexi Giannoulias in the upcoming mayoral race, signaling a split in the city’s progressive labor movement. Local 73 President Dian Palmer said Giannoulias would support union contracts for public employees and help win negotiations, contrasting with the union’s previous support for Mayor Brandon Johnson in 2024. The endorsement follows a dispute with the Chicago Teachers Union over organizing efforts and comes as SEIU locals have contributed more than $4.5 million to Johnson’s 2023 campaign.

items.title: District 7A school board race: Jesus Ayala Jr. picks up a local endorsement
items.summary: POLITICO's Illinois Playbook reports that District 7A school board candidate Jesus Ayala Jr. has been endorsed by the 34th Ward alderman. The note ran in the Playbook's Business of Politics roundup alongside other down-ballot races. Chicago's elected school board races are on the Nov. 3 ballot.

items.summary: Scott Olson/Getty Images Mayor Brandon Johnson's head tax will rise again in his 2027 budget - albeit with tweaks - in a plan he's scheduled to unveil today. The revived head tax, along with a higher cloud computing tax and $480 million in borrowing to pay off police settlements, could face stiff resistance from alders. items.summary: The Community Commission for Public Safety and Accountability will hold a public meeting on October 29. items.summary: A Halloween celebration will take place at Mary Bartelme Park on October 31 from 9:30 to 11:30 a.m. The event includes live music, a balloon artist, and other family‑friendly spooky surprises. The 34th Ward team and the park advisory council are hosting the festivities for the community.

items.summary: A suspect was in custody Tuesday morning after shots were fired near the Kluczynski Federal Building in downtown Chicago. Darius Johnson reports.

items.summary: All signs point to a 2028 presidential run for Gov. JB Pritzker, though he has not announced it. items.summary: Governor JB Pritzker signaled renewed optimism that negotiations will keep the Chicago Bears at their current stadium, countering GOP challenger Darren Bailey’s claim the team may move to Indiana. Stadium negotiators have hinted at momentum as the election approaches.

items.title: Mayoral poll shows mixed support for Mayor Brandon Johnson ahead of 2027 election
items.summary: A new poll released as mayoral candidates filed petitions shows many Chicago voters remain dissatisfied with Mayor Brandon Johnson’s performance and that likely voters express limited enthusiasm for his reelection bid. The poll was reported by the Chicago Tribune.

items.summary: IGWL and Chicago Sip & Paint are hosting a ticketed paint-and-sip holiday fundraiser on Wednesday, Nov. 18, from 6 to 8:30 p.m., with proceeds going to a local organization. The group's book club will also meet in person on Nov. 11 to discuss its next selection.

items.title: Kansas Senate race could end a 94-year Republican winning streak
items.summary: POLITICO Forecast reports that Kansas, which has not elected a Democratic senator since 1932, is in play two weeks before the Nov. 3 midterms. Democrats need a net gain of four seats to win back the Senate.
